tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a fresh hobby knife blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat. For stubborn cases, replace the decal and reapply with stronger solutions like Daco Strong.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kits Using Acetone
tips.text: To remove old paint from plastic kit parts, use acetone. Dip a cotton swab in acetone, gently rub the painted surface. Be careful not to oversaturate the plastic. For stubborn paint, use a toothbrush to scrub gently. After paint is removed, wash the part with warm soapy water and let dry. Apply a light coat of Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to seal the plastic before painting again.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts with Super Glue
tips.text: Breakage in photo-etch parts can be repaired using super glue (CA glue). Apply a small drop of glue on the join, align the parts, and press gently. Hold for 10 seconds. Let it dry for 15-20 seconds, then clean with a sharp hobby knife. Use accelerator for faster drying. For a seamless join, apply a thin layer of Vallejo Metal Color paint after repair.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes with Iwata Cleaner
tips.text: Airbrush clogs can be cleared using Iwata Cleaner. Disassemble the airbrush, soak the nozzle and needle in cleaner for 15 minutes. Scrub with a toothbrush, rinse with water, and reassemble. If clog persists, use a needle gauge to clean the needle. For serious clogs, use a needle file and magnifying glass. Always test spray after cleaning to ensure proper function.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Plastic Parts with Hot Water Bath
tips.text: Warped plastic parts can be corrected using a hot water bath. Soak the part in hot (but not boiling) water for 10 minutes. Gently bend the part back into shape while in water. Let it cool and dry naturally. For complex shapes, consider using a makeshift mold or support while drying. Avoid sudden temperature changes to prevent re-warping.
